Why no, no it's not. I traded mine for a real TV just yesterday - identical refresh rate, identical resolution, identical contrast ratio, same size, everything. It's fucking awesome! No wifi, no apps, no boot time (other than time to warm up the screen or whatever, like 3 seconds).

Honestly from what I've seen, most of the Smart TVs on the market aren't worth the cost you pay for them anyway. You can usually get a TV with the same specs, sans the smart features, for $100 - $200 less. You could then just buy a set-top box like a Roku for ~$50 and have the same features.

Completely agree. Except that I have owned 3 different models of the Roku and they are terrible. I don't know if it's the software being a big wad of bloat ot what, but they are laggy as fuck, they take forever to boot, and they crash at least twice a week in my experience. The interface is laggy, it's just terrible. I bought a Nexus Player a few months back and bought the gamepad with it ($50 total) and it's been the best set top purchase I've ever made.

You're right, of course. Roku has a lot of promise but I've had much the same experience as you. Personally I use a Chromecast (the baby brother of the Nexus Player) and an older tablet to replicate those features. I've been thinking about upgrading to the Nexus Player for the gaming aspects, though.

I will say, the gaming aspects aren't the best. Not bad, but not terribly great. I only have a couple of android games installed, where it's at is the emulators. With snes9x I have had a massive blast playing S/NES oldies.

It has the full Chromecast capability rolled in as well (I have a chromecast as well), and the Nexus Player performs so much better. It is seriously the best $25 bucks I have ever spent on an entertainment product.

I use Plex to stream my backups, and with the plex app it is the best media server+client experience I've ever seen. If you have plex or another media server on your pc/in your home, I would strongly suggest grabbing a Nexus Player. It's absolutely fantastic.
